newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Afrox unit buys three S.African hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Afrox unit buys three S.African hospitals.

text.p: South Africa's Afrox Healthcare, a unit of African Oxygen Ltd (Afrox), said on Friday it had bought three more hospitals, strengthening its position in the private healthcare market.

The group said in a statement it had bought the operating assets of the Vincent Pallotti Hospital in Cape Town, the Springsmed hospital in the Gauteng province town of Springs, and the James Hospital in East London in the Eastern Cape province.
Dick Williamson, general manager of Afrox Healthcare, said the purchase prices would not be revealed at this stage.
He told Reuters that the Cape Town purchase took effect on March 1, while agreements on the other two had been signed this week with their takeovers retrospective to March 1.
The acquisitions raise the total number of hospitals and day clinics owned by the firm to 18. It also has minority stakes in five other hospitals.
Afrox on Thursday announced flat half year earnings at 33.1 cents a share from 31.4 at the halfway stage last year amid a slower and more competitive trading environment.
It said business conditions were expected to remain difficult in the second half of the year.
